The workbook's own 'Definitions' tab defines the 'Pipeline Operator Name' field as 'Name of the natural gas transmission pipeline operators', i.e. EIA classifies every project in this dataset, this one included, as belonging to a natural gas transmission pipeline system.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded PipelineType=transmission confirmed: this EIA government dataset tracks natural gas TRANSMISSION pipeline projects by its own field definition ('Pipeline Operator Name' = 'natural gas transmission pipeline operators'), and its row for this exact expansion (matching name, operator, date, and capacity) sits inside that dataset. Independently, the physical facts in both press accounts — a >2,000-mile-network mainline expansion adding 400 MMcf/d via compression to reach 2.5 Bcf/d total capacity, serving industrial/LDC/LNG offtake across a multi-county corridor — describe large-diameter, long-haul mainline transport, not a gathering or distribution line. Only one distinct document available (the operator press releases don't use the word 'transmission'); flagging that a second, independently-authored source using the literal word was not found, though the government classification is unambiguous. NOTE: this EIA workbook's OWN 'Pipeline Type' column (a different field, Interstate/Intrastate FERC-jurisdiction) lists this specific row as 'Intrastate' — that is a distinct concept (regulatory jurisdiction, not transmission/gathering/distribution class) and does not conflict with GEM's PipelineType=transmission.
